questions.heading: The Ratio Is a Price, So It Depends on the Units
questions.stem: A water utility's model stores NPV in $k and avoided flood damage in $M, and maximizes 0.5 × NPV + 0.5 × avoided damage. What exchange rate has the model been given?

options.text: $1k of NPV is worth $1k of avoided damage, since the two weights are equal
options.says: Equal weights on different units are not equal prices: one unit of each adds 0.5, and the units are $1k and $1M.

options.text: $1k of NPV is worth $1,000k of avoided damage, since one unit of each adds 0.5
options.says: Right: $1k of NPV and $1M of avoided damage each add 0.5, so the model trades them one for one, as the $M row of the lesson showed.

options.text: $1k of avoided damage is worth $1,000k of NPV, since one unit of each adds 0.5
options.says: This inverts the rate: the unit worth 0.5 on the damage side is $1M, so damage is the cheap one per $k.

options.text: No rate at all yet, since weights only mean something after normalizing
options.says: Every weighted sum sets a price, whether or not the objectives were normalized; normalizing only changes which price.

questions.heading: The Plan Moves in Jumps as the Weights Change
questions.stem: In a project-selection MILP, shares of 0.30 and 0.55 on the first objective return the same plan. The board moves its share from 0.30 to 0.45. Which plan should it expect?

options.text: The same plan, since a plan best at two shares is best at every share between them
options.says: Right: each plan's score is a straight line in the share, so the plan on top at both ends of the range stays on top between them.

options.text: A plan between the old one and the next, since the share moved partway along
options.says: The plan only changes at a break-even share; there is no plan halfway, as the 101-weighting sweep showed.

options.text: A plan with more of the second objective, since its share rose
options.says: Its share fell, from 0.70 to 0.55, and inside the range the plan does not change at all.

options.text: A different plan, since every change of weights changes the plan
options.says: The sweep returned 8 plans for 101 weightings; most changes of weights change nothing.

questions.heading: Positive Weights Give a Pareto-Optimal Plan
questions.stem: A model maximizes cost savings and emissions cut with weights (1, 0). What can you promise about the plan it returns?

options.text: No plan beats it on either measure, though one may tie its savings
options.says: A plan that ties its savings and cuts more emissions beats it on emissions; with a zero weight that plan is not ruled out.

options.text: No plan ties its savings, though one may cut more emissions
options.says: Ties on the one counted objective are exactly what a zero weight allows; nothing makes the optimum unique.

options.text: No plan beats it in any way, though one may match it on both
options.says: A plan that ties its savings and cuts more is better in one way and no worse in the other; only positive weights rule that out.

options.text: No plan beats it on both, though one may tie it and cut more
options.says: Right: the plan is weakly Pareto optimal; a tied plan with more emissions cut can dominate it.
